lessons: Bloodline Keeper (2BB) and Victim of Night (1BB) sat on 7 Swamps in my WB; the guide warns BB needs 8+ sources, so count pips before the 10/7 split.
My WB had only two evasive threats, Chapel Geist and Bloodline Keeper, and lost 0-2 to WG in 24 and 36 turns; take a third flier or flier answer over another ground body.
Contradicting the guide's 45% WB line, seat 3's WB went 3-0 with Angelic Overseer, Rebuke and Victim of Night, beating my WB 2-1; WB works with fliers and removal.
Round 1 and Round 3 were long grinds of 14 to 29 turns, both lost 1-2, so prioritize cheap creatures and early pressure over slow spells like Lost in the Mist and Claustrophobia.
Seat 2's BR deck with Kessig Wolf and Vampire Interloper lost 2-0 in 12 and 17 turns, so value fast two-drops to punish aggressive draws.
Festerhide Boar came back at pick 8 and I played two, so take green bodies from packs 1 and 3 before more blue spells like Dissipate or Think Twice.
The guide calls BR vampires aggressive, but my ground-heavy Kessig Wolf, Markov Patrician and Night Revelers deck stalled in 18-26 turn games; take Vampire Interloper and Rakish Heir over them.
I took Claustrophobia second in pack 2, never played it, and then UG beat me 0-2 with it; commit to a lane by mid pack 2 rather than taking a card you won't play.
Expect answers: UG's Claustrophobia, Lost in the Mist and Dissipate, and WB's Rebuke and Victim of Night, so keep removal for their fliers and blockers.
Ghoulraiser and Abattoir Ghoul were the recurring threats in my 2-1 WB deck, so take the first Abattoir Ghoul early and take a second Ghoulraiser when offered.
Rebuke and Victim of Night were my only real removal, and cutting Champion of the Parish for its thin Human count left the deck short on answers, so take removal over tribal creatures.
My games ran 18 to 31 turns, so Moan of the Unhallowed's extra bodies were worth more than early aggression, and the next drafter should value grindy card advantage.
Tonight contradicted the guide's flier-first advice: my WG with four fliers went 1-6 in games, losing 12- and 22-turn games to BR, so cheap early plays matter more than flier count.
With green as my deeper colour I ran only 9 Forest and 7 Plains, fewer Forests than the guide's 10/7 WG split that went 3-0; take 10 sources for the main colour.
My WG spent early picks on two Dead Weights, Riot Devils and two Vampiric Furies and played none, confirming the guide's stranded-removal warning; commit to two colours by mid pack 1.

Take a second finisher over another bounce spell: your 24-, 31- and 20-turn games suggest Grasp of Phantoms, Silent Departure and Lost in the Mist bought time without closing, so Galvanic Juggernaut carried too much.
Fiend Hunter, your first pick, ended up in seat 4's WG deck, so an early pick you won't play can still feed an opponent. Commit to colours by mid pack 1 and pick playables from there.
Seat 3's WB deck beat you 2-1 with fliers and removal (Angelic Overseer, Falkenrath Noble, Victim of Night), so value cheap removal over another two-drop body like Village Ironsmith.
Value evasive fliers above Mask of Avacyn: my WG deck had almost no way over the board, and I lost round 1 0-2 to UR fliers in 20- and 28-turn games.
The guide's tempo-first advice underperformed here: five of six games ran 20-plus turns, so grindy removal like Rebuke and Spidery Grasp decided games more than early curves.

Spend early picks on removal and efficient creatures: Sensory Deprivation, Harvest Pyre, Brimstone Volley and two Makeshift Maulers carried my deck, while the three Curses I took in pack 1 were all cut.
Prioritise answers to fliers: seat 5's UR deck beat me 2-0 with Stitched Drake, Murder of Crows and Silent Departure, so value Sensory Deprivation and Frightful Delusion highly.
Take Ashmouth Hound early: I picked two in pack 2 and both made my deck, alongside Moon Heron and Mindshrieker as evasive threats.
